title: Usage Onramp Synchronizer and Adaptive Schema Sculptor
creator: Sofia Patel
description: We observe intermittent rejections and silent schema coercions when vine-like feature flags and ad-hoc client fields arrive during high-throughput console telemetry bursts. This ticket implements a two-part service: a lightweight synchronizer at the onramp that aligns tenant-level schema expectations with the schema registry and an 'Adaptive Schema Sculptor' that performs deterministic, reversible transformations for common drift cases (extra fields, legacy enum aliases, and timestamp format variants). The goal is to reduce P50 ingestion errors for console usage events from 0.8% to <0.1% while preserving strictness for high-risk fields (billing identifiers, event_type).
acceptance_criteria: Synchronizer fetches per-tenant schema version and compares hashes within 100ms for 99th percentile onramp latency
Sculptor rule engine applies deterministic transforms (enum alias mapping, timestamp normalization, deprecated-field rename) with audit metadata attached
Events failing sculptor rules are routed to a quarantine topic with explanatory reason and a unique rejection token
End-to-end pipeline shows ingestion error rate <0.1% on a synthetic burst test of 50k events/min with mixed schema versions
Server-side metrics include breakdown by transform type and tenant; dashboards created in Grafana and linked in PR
design_notes: Keep synchronizer stateless; cache schema fingerprints in a small LRU for 30s to avoid registry hotloops
Implement sculptor as a chain of composable rule transforms with explicit ordering and reversible metadata so rollbacks are safe
Make sculptor rules declarative (YAML) per tenant group; store canonical rules in the config service and validate via schema CI
For high-volume tenants, add an opt-in 'lenient mode' flag in tenant configuration to trade strictness for throughput
We avoid automatic addition of new fields into the canonical schema — sculptor must annotate, not mutate registry
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to processing stage (non-production) with full telemetry for two days
2) Canary with 5% of console traffic for two hours, monitor error rate, latency, and quarantine volume
3) Gradual ramp to 25% and then 100% while keeping opt-out toggles per tenant
4) Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window and automated backfill job for quarantined events with updated sculptor rules
testing_plan: Unit tests for each transform rule and round-trip reversibility tests
Integration test using the ingest harness to replay historical event batches with known drift patterns
Chaos test: inject malformed enums and timestamp variants to validate quarantine and metrics
Load test: 50k events/min mixed-tenants profile with 95th percentile processing latency under 250ms
